Explain the value of Cloudflare's platform: Connect commercial-segment customers' business and technical problems to the right Cloudflare products, such as Application Security and Performance, Zero Trust/SASE and the Developer Platform, and show the value they'd get. Work closely with other teams: Partner with Solutions Engineers on technical validation, and with the Partner Organisation to co-sell and close deals faster. Work with Marketing and BDR teammates on campaigns and events that create pipeline. Run your territory with data: Keep your Salesforce pipeline accurate and your forecasts reliable, track your activity and conversion numbers, and use what you learn to consistently meet or exceed your targets Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience: 1 - 3 years of experience in a sales role, preferably in SaaS or tech sales, such as:  BDR/SDR background with strong outbound experience in a high-paced environment SMB or Transactional sales experience with high volume, high velocity sales motion Strong track record of meeting or exceeding quota  Strong discovery and qualification skills using frameworks like BANT, MEDDIC  Excellent presentation and interpersonal communication skills (verbal and written) as well as time management skill Experience using CRM like Salesforce, outbound/prospecting sales tools (e.g. LinkedIn Sales Navigator, ZoomInfo, Salesforce Sales Engagement Outreach etc) Tech-savvy and technically curious - quick to learn technical products, comfortable to run live demos independently, data-driven mindset   Highly accountable and self-driven, customer-centric individuals Multilingual abilities (depending on the coverage regions) What Makes Cloudflare Special? We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost. Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states. 1.1.1.1 : We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers. Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you! descriptionAr: About the Team The Supply Chain Technology team within OpenAI's Enterprise Platform & Technology organization builds the systems and data foundations that support our supply chain and partner operations. We connect enterprise applications, improve operational visibility, and automate workflows across planning, purchasing, manufacturing, inventory, fulfillment, and returns. We work closely with engineering and business teams to build reliable systems that can evolve with OpenAI's growth. About the Role We are seeking an Integrations Architect to set technical direction for enterprise integrations, with a strong focus on supply chain and external partner ecosystems. You will help evolve a growing integration portfolio into a scalable, maintainable foundation through clear architecture, reusable patterns, and strong engineering practices. You will also help establish shared integration architecture and reusable foundations needed to support Finance and Supply Chain systems. This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will translate business processes into integration designs, evaluate existing implementations, challenge assumptions, and guide improvements from design through production. Your influence will extend across application engineers, integration engineers, platform teams, and business stakeholders. You will own integration architecture and partner with the engineering team responsible for the shared integration platform. Through clear requirements, working implementations, and operational evidence, you will help shape capabilities that improve how integrations are developed, tested, deployed, observed, and recovered. In this role, you will: Own integration architecture across enterprise applications, custom services, and external partners, including e-commerce platforms, logistics providers, contract manufacturers, retailers, and distributors. Translate supply chain processes into clear system boundaries, transaction flows, data ownership, interface contracts, and operational requirements. Partner with Finance and engineering teams to establish reusable integration patterns connecting operational and financial systems, with clear data ownership, reconciliation, and auditability. Assess existing integrations and lead a practical modernization roadmap that improves scalability, reliability, maintainability, and cost while sustaining business delivery. Establish reference architectures, reusable connectors, API and event standards, data mappings, versioning practices, and documented design decisions. Lead design and code reviews and mentor engineers. Select appropriate API, messaging, EDI, orchestration, and batch patterns, balancing platform capabilities with custom development and the needs of each business process. Stay close to implementation by building Python services and reference solutions, reviewing code, resolving difficult production issues, and validating designs through tests and measurable behavior. Define reliability and recovery patterns, including idempotency, retries, reconciliation, replay, and continuity planning. Establish operational objectives and ownership across system boundaries. Enable observability that follows business transactions across systems, connecting technical execution to business outcomes and supporting diagnosis, safe recovery, and ongoing improvement. Turn integration delivery experience into prioritized platform requirements and influence shared engineering roadmaps through prototypes, acceptance criteria, and evidence of value. Enable effective AI-assisted development and agentic workflows through well-defined interfaces, testable behavior, explicit approvals, and controls over execution and cost. Apply MCP tools, plugins, or comparable approaches where useful. Embed security, access controls, segregation of duties, auditability, and change management into integration design. Coordinate partner testing, cutover, and operational readiness. You might thrive in this role if you: Bring 10+ years of experience in enterprise integration engineering and architecture, including technical leadership for business-critical systems. Understand supply chain processes well enough to independently translate purchasing, receiving, order management, fulfillment, and inventory needs into integrations and explain the operational impact of missing or incorrect transactions. Can support integrations across Supply Chain & Finance systems, working with subject matter experts to translate business processes, reconciliation needs, and financial controls into reliable designs. Have personally shaped architectures, improved existing implementations, and guided engineers toward reusable, maintainable solutions with measurable results. Have deep experience across multiple integration platforms and approaches, including iPaaS and custom services, and can translate their strengths and limitations into useful platform requirements. Are a strong Python engineer who can connect design recommendations to production code, automated tests, deployment practices, and troubleshooting. Understand API and event design, asynchronous messaging, EDI, data contracts, authentication, transaction integrity, and failure recovery across distributed systems. Have built and operated high-volume integrations and can reason about performance, capacity, reliability, observability, and operating cost. Are comfortable with cloud infrastructure, containerized services, version control, CI/CD, and automated integration testing. Can influence technical direction across teams, explain tradeoffs to business stakeholders, and mentor engineers without relying on reporting authority. Work independently, navigate ambiguity, and take responsibility for outcomes from initial design through sustained operation. Preferred Qualifications Integrations with Oracle Fusion ERP or SCM and adjacent enterprise applications such as warehouse, transportation, planning, or product lifecycle management systems. Shapi

You’ll focus on the broad base of startups beyond our sales team’s 1:1 coverage, creating engagement approaches that help founders and developers discover our products, get started, and deepen their adoption over time. This role combines growth marketing, field marketing, online events, content, and ecosystem partnerships. You’ll connect these activities into a coherent journey from a startup’s first interaction with OpenAI to sustained product usage and revenue growth. You’ll join the APAC Startups team and work closely with sales, technical, marketing, developer relations, and partnerships colleagues. In this role, you’ll: Own growth across startups beyond active sales coverage. Create programs that move founders and developers from initial interest to their first working use case, production deployment, and broader adoption. Run field and online programs. Design founder gatherings, technical workshops, hackathons, webinars, and other formats with clear audiences, follow-up journeys, and measurable outcomes. Collaborate with Marketing to create useful content. Work with technical experts, marketers, and customers to produce practical guides, demos, startup stories, and campaigns that help teams solve problems and build with OpenAI. Develop lifecycle campaigns. Use email, digital channels, and product and engagement signals to deliver relevant guidance at key moments in a startup’s journey. Extend our reach through partners. Collaborate with venture capital firms, accelerators, startup communities, and other ecosystem partners to reach and support founders at scale. Prioritize across APAC. Segment audiences by market, stage, use case, and adoption maturity, adapting programs to local needs while building formats that can be reused across the region. Connect growth programs to sales. Establish clear signals and handoffs for startups that would benefit from direct commercial or technical support. Measure and improve performance. Own a dashboard spanning activation, sustained usage, revenue growth, retention, and program efficiency. Use experiments and cohort analysis to identify what works and where to invest. Own execution. Manage the program calendar, budget, agencies, and vendors, balancing ambitious goals with disciplined delivery. We’re seeking someone with: 6+ years of experience in growth, lifecycle, developer, or field marketing for a technology business, ideally serving startups or developers. A track record of turning campaigns and programs into measurable product adoption and revenue growth. Experience combining events, content, digital channels, and lifecycle marketing into an integrated growth motion. Strong analytical judgment: you can define success, interpret funnel and cohort data, and distinguish activity from business impact. Strong writing and storytelling skills, with the ability to make technical topics useful and accessible to founders and builders. Experience working across APAC, with an understanding of how startup ecosystems, languages, and routes to market vary across the region. The ability to work effectively with sales, technical teams, marketing, and ecosystem partners. An ownership mindset and the willingness to move between strategy and hands-on execution. descriptionAr: About Omni Omni is the AI analytics platform that turns company data into a trusted source of truth for AI. Built on a semantic model, Omni gives teams a governed context graph, so everyone gets the same trusted answer. Ask in plain English, refine in workbooks, or bring your data into tools like Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and Slack. Our team has spent decades building data platforms, and we started Omni to fix problems we saw firsthand. Today, we help customers like Condé Nast, BambooHR, and Synthesia get better answers from their data. We're headquartered in San Francisco and have raised $217M from top investors including ICONIQ, Theory Ventures, and Redpoint Ventures. Our latest $120M Series C valued us at $1.5B. If you like helping people get more from their data, come build with us. We’d love to hear from you. About the Role As a Solutions Engineer, you'll be a trusted technical expert on the Omni platform, empowering customers to do more with their data throughout the customer lifecycle. You'll own the technical side of every deal — building one shared plan with your Account Executive and leading complex technical evaluations from discovery through proof-of-concept, hands-on in each prospect's own data and environment. You'll drive each evaluation forward, bring a clear point of view, and help shape product direction with feedback from the field. Responsibilities Partner with the Sales team to provide technical expertise in the sales process and beyond, helping uncover and prove out use cases to showcase the value of the Omni platform. Build and present Proofs of Concept (POCs) in the Omni Platform as part of the evaluation process, enabling prospective customers on how to successfully use Omni on their data. Smoothly transition trials into successful customers by partnering with post-sales teams and engaging with our partners to plan for ongoing support where needed. Collaborate extensively with Product, Design, and Engineering to provide user feedback and guide product direction. About You 7+ years of experience in data analytics or business intelligence, with strong customer-facing communication skills. Pre-sales experience is preferred but not required if you have extensive experience in the BI space. Strong SQL skills, using SQL for analytics. Familiarity with the modern data stack, including cloud data warehouses (e.g. Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift) and transformation tools (e.g. dbt). Comfortable owning technical conversations directly with customers. Passionate about working with data; love learning, and enthusiastic about helping and teaching others. Prior experience with business intelligence and/or enterprise data analytics tools (such as Looker, Omni, Tableau, PowerBI, Mode, Sisense, etc). Experience at a high-growth, Series A-D startup is preferred. Location This is a fully remote role open to candidates based anywhere in the US. Why Join Us Passionate, supportive team with extensive experience in the space (including founders from Looker and Stitch Data) all working together to win as a team Employer paid health, dental, and vision insurance 401(k) Plan Flexible PTO Omni is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and encourage you to apply even if you don’t check every single box. Please, let us know if you need any reasonable accommodations during the interview process.

descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineeriIng teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works. Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere. About the Role As a Mid-Market Enterprise Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations. This is a rare opportunity to work as one of the early hires for a new segment within Applied AI Engineering, contributing real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve. This role is based in Singapore. Independently define and refine your team’s strategy, priorities, and operating model, aligning company priorities, customer needs, and the Singapore go-to-market while balancing near-term execution with long-term team capability. Partner with Sales leadership and Account Directors to prioritise accounts and opportunities, make complex resource-allocation decisions, and establish clear technical strategies for your team’s portfolio. Build a culture that balances ambitious customer outcomes with responsible AI deployment, clear ownership, thoughtful prioritisation, and effective specialist handoffs. descriptionAr: The Role Our commercial segment — companies with up to 500 employees — is predominantly developer- and engineer-led. These buyers don't respond to decks and discovery scripts. They respond to someone who speaks their language, understands their architecture, and can help them think through a real problem. That's who we're hiring. As a Commercial Account Executive at ClickHouse, you'll own the full sales cycle for inbound, product-led, and self-serve accounts in this segment. You'll engage with data engineers, platform teams, and technical founders at the moment they're evaluating ClickHouse for a real use case — and your job is to help them succeed, faster. The best deals in this segment don't feel like sales. They feel like an engineering consultation that ends in a contract. Our commercial customers include companies like Applied Compute , Instinct , WorkOS , Prime Intellect , Browserbase , Temporal , TypeSafe AI , and Blacksmith — developer-first products that chose ClickHouse because they needed something that could handle billions of events without slowing down their users. The best deals in this segment don't feel like sales. They feel like an engineering consultation that ends in a contract. This is a role for technically strong people who are ready to own a number. You'll need at least 1-2 years of closing experience, and technical credibility is non-negotiable. What You Will Be Doing Own the full sales cycle from inbound lead to close for accounts in the sub-250 employee segment, with a focus on speed, technical depth, and conversion quality. Engage directly with data engineers, platform architects, and technical founders to understand their use cases, data volumes, query patterns, and infrastructure requirements — and map those to ClickHouse capabilities. Troubleshoot schema design questions, ingestion patterns, and integration challenges during the evaluation process; serve as a trusted technical advisor rather than a traditional sales rep. Identify expansion opportunities within the existing self-serve and product-led customer base; convert usage signals into meaningful commercial relationships. Partner with Solutions Engineers on more complex evaluations, and advocate for customer needs internally with Product and Engineering. Maintain rigorous pipeline hygiene — documenting technical context, decision criteria, stakeholders, and next steps in Salesforce so nothing falls through the cracks. Contribute to playbooks, technical objection handling guides, and onboarding materials that help the team scale what's working. Participate in developer community events, technical meetups, and online forums where our users naturally gather. What You Bring At least 1-2 years of closing experience carrying a quota, ideally selling technical or data infrastructure products to engineering buyers. A technical foundation that earns respect in engineering conversations — built through experience as a data engineer, solutions engineer/architect, software engineer, or similar role. Comfort with the modern data stack: columnar databases, streaming ingestion (Kafka, Kinesis), cloud infrastructure, and SQL-heavy analytics workflows. Hands-on experience with ClickHouse, DuckDB, Druid, Pinot, BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar is a strong plus. Some customer-facing experience — whether in pre-sales, technical account management, solutions engineering, or a customer-success capacity. You've navigated technical conversations with real stakes before. An instinct for moving quickly. This segment runs on short cycles. You know how to drive urgency without being pushy, and how to remove technical blockers that stall deals. Strong written and verbal communication. You can simplify complex concepts without dumbing them down, and you write clearly enough that your emails actually get responses from engineers. Curiosity about the business side of technology. You're interested in understanding why companies buy, not just what they're building. Ownership mentality. You're comfortable operating with autonomy, making judgment calls without a playbook, and learning from what doesn't work. Why This Role Is Different Most AE roles are execution roles. This one is a craft role. You'll build deep product knowledge, learn how high-growth companies architect for scale, and develop commercial skills in an environment where your technical instincts are your biggest competitive advantage. For the right person, this is a rare opportunity to bridge two worlds — and get paid competitively to do it. Perks Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries. Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare. Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity. Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries. A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee. Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites. Culture - We All Shape It As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture. Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here . Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse. Equal Opportunity & Privacy ClickHouse provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type based on factors such as race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. Please see here for our Privacy Statement.

descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Austin, TX (Hybrid) About the Department Emerging Technologies & Incubation (ETI) is where new and bold products are built and released within Cloudflare. Rather than being constrained by the structures which make Cloudflare a hugely successful business, we are able to leverage them to deliver entirely new tools and products to our customers. Cloudflare’s edge and network make it possible to solve problems at massive scale and efficiency which would be impossible for almost any other organization. About the Team We build the infrastructure that makes the web Payable , powering the future of machine-to-machine commerce. Here at Cloudflare, agentic commerce is a core part of our vision for the Agentic Internet . As AI agents increasingly navigate, consume, and act on the web, standard payment and authorization models built for humans are breaking down. We are building tools that help make the new internet payable by giving our users the ability to take control over how AI agents pay for resources across the Internet. Building these capabilities requires solving problems across high-throughput web infrastructure, low-latency transaction processing, digital wallets, and emerging agentic payment protocols. We bridge mainstream fiat commerce rails with decentralized protocols, enabling micro-payments at Internet scale. We’re looking for someone excited to deliver products so domain owners can control this experience, while identifying the problems Cloudflare is uniquely positioned to solve next. We are a tight-knit group that communicates and collaborates regularly. We celebrate our achievements, support each other when we make mistakes, and hold each other and our work to a high standard. About the role We are looking for an Engineering Manager to build and lead the engineering team across Agentic Commerce. You will be responsible for the people, execution, and engineering quality behind products that power machine-to-machine payments and monetization, such as our Monetization Gateway . You will partner closely with Product Management and engineering teams across Cloudflare to deliver current priorities and shape future opportunities. This is a management role for someone who is deeply technically credible. You will not be expected to write most of the code, but you should be able to understand the systems your engineers operate, challenge architectural decisions around payment rails and cryptographic auth, ask the right questions when something is going wrong, and step into a technical problem when the situation calls for it. At the same time, we are looking for a manager, not a tech lead with direct reports. Your success will be measured by the quality and output of the team you build, the engineers you develop, and the systems and products they deliver. This role may require flexibility to be on-call outside of standard working hours to address technical issues as needed. What you'll do Manage, coach, and grow engineers working across high-throughput payment pipelines, agent authentication, and web-scale commerce architecture. Own execution by establishing clear priorities, creating predictable delivery, and giving engineers the context and autonomy to own meaningful areas of the product. Lead the development of agentic payment systems leveraging emerging open standards (x402, Web Bot Auth, ACP, UCP) to enable low-latency, machine-to-machine micropayments. Lead the engineering behind usage metering, pricing definition engines, outcome verification, and revenue attribution models tailored for agentic workflows. Build capabilities that give businesses granular visibility and control over their agent-generated revenue streams. Partner closely with Product Management to understand customer problems, shape the roadmap, and turn broad opportunities into clear engineering outcomes. Bridge mainstream and decentralized tech, interfacing with blockchain teams while keeping execution focused on mainstream, high-throughput web and fiat commerce rails. Balance near-term product delivery with thoughtful technical investments that allow promising ideas to grow. Own the operational health of the systems in your area, including observability, incident response, cryptographic security, and long-term reliability. Develop technical leaders and create space for engineers to lead architecture and implementation. Responsibilities We want you to love it here. This role is a g

descriptionAr: Developers decide what’s interesting long before they decide what to buy. They follow builders, share the talk everyone is watching, and argue about benchmarks in the replies. Most infrastructure brands show up in that feed looking and sounding the same. ClickHouse has the material to do something different: a fast, open-source database that has grown into a platform for real-time analytics, data warehousing, observability, and AI workloads; engineers and leaders with real points of view; and a brand that already turns up in unexpected places, from a Premier League partnership to our own Open House conference. We are looking for a Senior Social Media Manager to run the ClickHouse accounts and turn that material into a brand developers actually want to follow, at the intersection of infrastructure, technology, and culture. You’ll own our presence on LinkedIn, X, and YouTube with video at the center: clipping talks, podcasts, launches, and live moments into content that travels, building formats people come back for, and working with the creators developers already trust. You’ll be accountable for growing audience and engagement across a global community. You’ll sit on the Story & Communications team, reporting to the Head of Story & Communications, and work closely with developer relations, product marketing, demand generation, events, and our brand and design team. This is a hands-on role: you’ll make the work, not only schedule it. for a global audience across time zones Put video at the center of how ClickHouse shows up: clip talks, podcasts, livestreams, launches, and executive moments into short-form and vertical content, and opinion, and craft Work with the creators and technical voices developers already follow, through collaborations, co-created content, guest appearances, and amplification, in tandem with developer relations and the wider marketing team Turn launches, announcements, customer stories, and research into social moments, and bring live coverage from Open House and industry events, working with regional teams so local moments reach a global audience Grow the voices around the brand: partner with communications on executive presence on LinkedIn and X, and give employees and developer advocates what they need to share their work Own the numbers for organic social, including audience growth, engagement, video performance, and share of the developer conversation, and report on what’s working and why Track what developers say about ClickHouse and the category and feed it back to product marketing, developer relations, and campaign teams, while using AI tooling and a lean production workflow to ship content quickly and partnering with demand generation so the best organic work gets paid reach What You Bring Along A record of growing audience and engagement at scale for a brand with a global following, and the numbers to show it Real fluency with video: you can shoot, edit, and clip yourself, you know what makes short-form and vertical content work on each platform, and you can find the best ninety seconds in an hour-long talk Experience running influencer or creator programs: finding the right voices, structuring partnerships, and making the collaboration feel native to the creator’s audience Experience with a technical or B2B audience, and the ability to turn technical substance into something people want to share Preferred: experience in SaaS, developer tools, or infrastructure Taste and a point of view on internet culture: you know where developers spend time online, what they find funny, and what makes them tune a brand out Sharp short-form writing: the post, the hook, the caption, the thread A builder’s approach: you test quickly, read the data honestly, scale what works, and drop what doesn’t Comfort owning a channel end to end while working across many teams, with low ego and high standards Perks Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. About the Role We’re looking for an Optical Mechanical Engineer to design, prototype, and validate high-density fiber interconnects for our AI infrastructure. You’ll work across MT ferrule–based connectors and adapters, optical transceiver mechanical designs, tray-level optical assemblies, and fiber shuffle solutions, translating optical and system requirements into reliable, manufacturable hardware. This is a hands-on role spanning detailed mechanical design, lab testing, and integration. You’ll partner with optical, mechanical, networking, manufacturing, and data center teams to make fiber connections practical to assemble, route, test, and service—from within a tray or rack to the cabling infrastructure connecting racks. In this role, you will: Design and test MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters, addressing alignment, tolerances, retention, mating repeatability, and serviceability. Develop mechanical designs for optical transceivers and tray-level optical solutions, balancing packaging density, thermal interfaces, assembly access, and fiber management. Design and validate high-density fiber shuffle assemblies, including shuffle cassettes, with clear connectivity maps, controlled routing, and accessible test interfaces. Define and execute optical-mechanical validation plans, including optical loss measurements, connector inspection, mating cycles, and relevant environmental and mechanical testing. Develop fiber routing within and between racks, accounting for bend radius, strain relief, cable management, labeling, installation, and maintenance access. Partner with data center and network teams to translate fiber layouts and cabling infrastructure requirements into hardware interfaces and integration plans. Work with suppliers and manufacturing partners to build prototypes, resolve failures, improve assembly consistency, and transition validated designs into production. You might thrive in this role if you: You have hands-on experience designing and testing MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters. You have developed and tested fiber interconnects, including high-density fiber solutions, and can connect mechanical design decisions to optical performance. You have experience with the mechanical design and integration of optical transceivers and tray-level optical assemblies. You have designed and validated fiber shuffle solutions, such as shuffle cassettes, including connectivity, routing, assembly, and test considerations. You understand fiber routing within and between racks, including bend-radius constraints, strain relief, connector access, and serviceability. You are familiar with data center fiber layouts and the cabling infrastructure that supports installation, expansion, and operation. You can move between detailed design and hands-on debugging, use measurements to identify root causes, and work with engineering and manufacturing partners to implement practical improvements. descriptionAr: Hi, I’m Kayla :) I lead global community activation within Partnerships at Ashby. Before joining a year ago, I spent 15 years in TA and was an Ashby customer. I made the move out of TA into this role, and nothing I’d learned has gone to waste. If anything, I’ve learnt even more from the community. It’s genuinely one of the most rewarding and fun roles I’ve had, and as I step into a leadership role, I’m on the hunt for someone to take over the work in EMEA and evolve it further. We’re hiring an experienced TA Expert & Community Lead to grow one of our most successful GTM experiments: a high-touch, customer-led approach to growth. The model is already working in EMEA, built on curated events, product education and early community activation. You’ll own it across our target markets (UK&I, France, Nordics and Benelux), from customer breakfasts and curated experiences to enablement sessions and product demos. This role suits someone who has worked with Ashby All-in-One, has a solid background in TA, and cares about tools, process, hospitality and community building. It also works well for TA people who still love the work but want to use what they know somewhere new. You’ll work closely with Sales, CS and Product Marketing, own a region end-to-end, and see how community connects to pipeline and retention. A quick summary on travel, since it’s usually the first question and we know it means time away from home: you’ll have events in London regularly, plus one trip to another EMEA city a month, usually for around four days. Busier periods can mean two trips abroad in a month. There is flex, though. I’m a mum of three, and in this role, I’ve been able to stay home and take meaningful time off during every school holiday. We plan the calendar well in advance, so you’ll know what’s coming and can sort things at home with plenty of notice. It’s also one of the best parts of the job. I’ve met some amazing people and had some really cool experiences along the way, from hosting a dinner cruise on the Seine and a TA leader workshop with a partner at the Shangri-La Paris, to spending time in customers’ offices in Stockholm, our company offsite in Playa Del Carmen, and hosting the mainstage at our first Ashby One London. What you’ll do Lead EMEA Community Events Run community events across target EMEA markets. Event types might include: Customer learning breakfasts A mixed ecosystem event for customers and prospects Partner cocktail events or roundtables co-hosted with local ecosystem players Build and nurture relationships with TA leaders Partner with Event Ops on venue selection, invites, and post-event recaps Drive improvement and reimagine how we can show up in a very meaningful way for the community Drive Customer Education Become an Expert in Ashby + TA leader needs to curate relevant content Design and lead live sessions that help customers activate key Ashby features and keep customers ahead on key TA trends and topics Partner with CS and Product Marketing teams on the Ashby Hidden Gems program Develop and distribute product tips, dashboards, and templates to increase customer sophistication Expand EMEA Community and Customer Advocacy Help Ashby deepen its brand and trust by showing up consistently and thoughtfully Participate in and help advise on content for ACE (Ashby Customer Expert) events when we bring the program to EMEA Partner with GTM teams on prospect and customer onsite visits Moderate panels, attend events, and build a presence at industry gatherings Who you’ll work with You’ll report directly to me, but work closely with myself and Willem , who has pioneered what community growth looks like at Ashby. Within partnerships, you’ll also work closely with Katie to scale trusted community partner relationships and Louise to bring Owned Community experiences, like Ashby Cafe , to life. You’ll also partner day to day with our EMEA Sales and CS teams, who know our customers and prospects best and help shape who we bring into the room. About You We think the ideal person for this role will have experience and skills that look something like this: You’ve been an Ashby power user or at least very familiar with Ashby and seen its benefits first-hand—someone who knows the product and Ashby community, champions good recruiting practices, and isn’t afraid to dive into dashboards, workflows, or templates You’ve built a reputation inside organizations as the go-to expert on TA process and tooling You’re a strong communicator—whether facilitating a breakfast, writing a post-event summary, or helping a customer understand how to build a dashboard You love curating and connecting people and ideas. You get energy from hosting, matchmaking, and finding smart formats to share what works You’re excited about being on the road ~2x/month and tapping into your existing network (and growing it!) in the TA space You have strong business acumen. You understand how community supports the wider business and work well with Sales and CS to make sure our programs are reaching the right people You’re entrepreneurial and experimental in nature. You’re not looking for rigid playbooks; you want room to try new formats and evolve what ‘great’ looks like. You come prepared with AI tools / automations that help us execute faster while maintaining quality. You believe in unreasonable hospitality—the idea that going above and beyond for a customer doesn’t just build goodwill, it builds momentum. This Role Probably Isn't Right If ... You’re not excited about hosting or don’t enjoy the details of curating small, thoughtful gatherings You hate writing and have difficulty building a cohesive brief (this is a very important skill at Ashby) You don’t enjoy travelling and building new connections while you’re at it You’ve never had hands-on TA experience You’ve never used Ashby and aren’t familiar with modern TA systems and practices You prefer working from a very established playbook and are uncomfortable with ambiguity or iteration

descriptionAr: About the team The Connectors team is the bridge between ClickHouse and the broader data ecosystem. We build and maintain the integrations that make ClickHouse accessible to millions of developers, data practitioners and AI agents worldwide: data visualization plugins (Tableau, Power BI, Superset, Metabase), connectors for data frameworks (Apache Spark, Flink, Kafka Connect, Beam, Fivetran), transformation and orchestration tooling (dbt, Airflow, Dagster), and AI tooling. Our work directly shapes how companies process massive datasets: real-time analytics platforms ingesting millions of events per second, observability systems monitoring global infrastructure, and the data warehouses and AI-powered applications redefining how teams work with data. We collaborate closely with the open-source community, internal teams, and enterprise users to ensure ClickHouse integrations set the standard for performance, reliability, and developer experience. About the role As a Senior Software Engineer focused on the data warehousing ecosystem, you will own how ClickHouse plugs into the modern analytics-engineering toolchain. This role sits at the intersection of high-performance database engineering, developer experience, and production operations. You will build the integrations that let data teams use ClickHouse as the warehouse behind the tools they already run, and you will own how those integrations are deployed and operated at scale. You will drive architecture, performance, and feature direction across four areas: Transformation: dbt, across both the Python-based v1 adapter and the Rust-based v2 (Fusion) engine; SQLMesh Semantic layer: dbt Semantic Layer / MetricFlow, Cube, Apache Ossie (formerly Open Semantic Interchange) Schema and metadata management: schema evolution, model contracts, migration tooling, catalog integration Orchestration: Apache Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, Temporal, and how transformation jobs run inside them (Astronomer Cosmos, dagster-dbt) We are looking for someone who has run the transformation layer of a real data warehouse, not just written models in it. You have operated dbt and its orchestration for many teams: CI/CD, environments, scheduling, credentials, observability, and cost. You know what breaks at scale because you were the one paged for it. You know what it takes to maintain code that other teams’ pipelines depend on – ideally because you’ve contributed to the open-source data warehousing ecosystem yourself (dbt and its adapters, orchestration providers, semantic-layer tooling or similar). You bring that practitioner's insight into what we should build and why, and you turn it into robust, production-ready integrations and the deployment artifacts (container images, Helm charts, reference architectures) that make ClickHouse the natural choice when data teams design their next warehouse. ClickHouse integrations for semantic-layer tooling (MetricFlow, Cube, Apache Ossie), making ClickHouse a first-class target for governed metrics consumed by BI tools and AI agents Build and maintain orchestration integrations (Airflow provider, Dagster, Prefect) and the patterns for running transformation jobs inside them Define how schema evolution, model contracts, and migrations work across running transformation and orchestration workloads on Kubernetes against ClickHouse Build and operate the Kubernetes-based CI, integration-test, and benchmark infrastructure Engage actively with the open-source community: triage issues, support contributors, advocate for users, and shape the roadmap from real-world feedback Collaborate with Product, Cloud, and core database teams to align integration work with broader priorities Bring a practitioner's perspective to roadmap decisions, grounding prioritization in how data and analytics engineers actually operate a warehouse About you 7+ descriptionAr: Hi, I’m Chris , and I lead Corporate Communications at Ashby. My career has been far from linear: I started in sports journalism, moved into Comms consulting, went in-house at a major bank to do Corporate Strategy, transitioned to a startup to build out their Content function, and earlier this year I joined Ashby’s Content team. The throughline between these roles is storytelling; whether it’s triple-A players to watch out for, how to tell a comprehensive story to investors, or best ways to showcase customer love, it all boils down to finding the most compelling narrative. What drew me to Ashby, in part, is the clarity of the product and audience. I was an Ashby customer for years as a hiring manager at Modern Treasury, so I saw firsthand how intentional this team is about building a product that makes hiring more effective, intuitive, and human. While I’ve led a content and comms team before, the function will look a little different at Ashby. As I build out our mandate with our Head of Content, Anum, I’m trying to be thoughtful about scope, strategy, audience, and delivery. We’re a growing team with high standards, and those standards should carry into how we communicate about Ashby as a whole. That brings me to this role, which I’ve owned since joining and am now evolving and “ giving away the legos .” We have a working case study program and a customer base that loves talking about us, and a healthy bench of talent leaders and RecOps practitioners willing to share organic, unprompted love for Ashby. We have come a long way on customer stories, but we’re still only a fraction of the way to what they could become. This role is about closing that gap by taking ownership of how our customers show up in the world. You’ll work across Marketing, Sales, and CS to scale our case study program, own enablement, and continuously improve the process of our customer content flywheel. In the near term, that means publishing a steady stream of written case studies; in the long term, you’ll define what a best-in-class in-depth customer story looks like at Ashby, from evaluation through implementation and beyond. Volume is important here, and so is depth, and the role is delivering on both. This role reports to me. I’m looking for someone with editorial taste, and the kind of curiosity that digs deep on how our product solves real TA problems, and a personable demeanor that makes a busy talent leader happy to spend an hour on the phone with you. If that sounds like you, please apply! What you’ll be responsible for in this role Own Ashby’s customer storytelling strategy. Building on a working case study program, you'll rethink our written stories and narratives with deeper operational detail that shows how great teams practice modern recruiting and the measurable, real-world impact of the product. Interview customers and write stories yourself, building the kind of trust that gets talent leaders to share the specific, messy details that make a story useful. Track how each story performs by channel and use what you learn to shape the next one. Work with internal partners on a plan for refreshing existing case studies and updating outdated ones. Partner with Marketing to bring the strongest stories into key brand moments like Ashby One. Work with our multimedia team on video and creative formats. You'll own the customer relationship and the story, and they'll own production, so the best customers end up in the most memorable formats. You'll bring editorial taste and a deep read on the TA zeitgeist to make stories that feel unmistakably Ashby. Collaborate with our Partnerships and CS teams to develop customer advocacy and reference programs. They run strategic activation for our talent community, and you'll make sure the content and resources that show up in their in-person activations and engagement campaigns are sharp, clear, and genuinely useful to the founders and talent leaders in the room. Establish clear systems for tracking advocacy contributions across content, product feedback, event participation, and references. Build a reference process that protects customer time while giving Sales, Marketing, and Comms access to the strength of our user base. Create meaningful ways to thank customers that stay objective and never cross ethical lines. Work with Partnerships on joint customer stories, partner references, and co-marketing. Partner with CS, Product, and RevOps so that insights and contributions flow back into the business. Capture and amplify organic love from the community. Each week, dozens of practitioners share unprompted stories about Ashby, our product, our sales cycle, our reliability, and our people. We capture some of it on our Ashby Wall of Love , but there's far more out there than we collect today. Turn sentiment into assets people use, from testimonial moments to themed compilations to category education pieces. Treat organic love as a sourcing channel, routing the best posts toward case studies, references, and employee content. Your work will help prospects and the broader TA world see what our customers experience every day. Help every team with customer story enablement. You'll build the enablement structure that helps GTM teams tell customer stories with confidence, so one great conversation can become employee posts, sales references, and community moments. An overview of this role As an Intermediate Security Engineer on GitLab's Security Incident Response Team (SIRT), you will be on the frontline of protecting both GitLab.com and GitLab the company from security threats. This role operates on a compressed 4-day work schedule, with a full-time week's hours condensed into four longer working days. Shifts run either Sunday through Wednesday or Wednesday through Saturday to provide 24/7/365 security coverage. This role also supports our FedRAMP environment and requires U.S. citizenship and residency within the United States. Your primary focus will be detecting and responding to security incidents during your scheduled shifts. You'll work extensively with our incident response automation tools to investigate, analyze, and resolve security events. You'll also use AI to build security tooling and automation, helping to improve our detection and response capabilities. In this role, you'll develop expertise using our security infrastructure to monitor for threats, analyze potential incidents, and coordinate response efforts across teams. This position is ideal for someone who wants to grow their incident response skills while working within GitLab's established security framework. You'll learn to think both tactically and strategically about security, while getting hands-on experience handling real-world incidents. Successful Security Engineers thrive in high-pressure environments, remaining calm while following prepared runbooks and thinking critically about security challenges. In this role, you will learn to think like both an attacker and defender, developing proactive and preventative security measures to keep GitLab and its users' data safe in our ever-changing threat landscape. Through hands-on experience and mentorship, you'll develop the skills needed to anticipate security risks, respond effectively to incidents, and contribute to GitLab's robust security posture. Find out more about the Security Operations team and responsibilities here: Incident Response Trust and Safety Red Team Threat-Intelligence Detection Engineering What you’ll do    Respond to and own security incidents in our 24/7 global rotation, managing them from detection through containment and recovery Create and maintain incident response documentation, including runbooks and standard procedures Contribute to post-incident analysis through RCA and lessons-learned reviews to strengthen our incident response program Build AI-assisted automation and tooling to improve operational efficiency and reduce manual work Drive continuous improvement by identifying security gaps and contributing to advanced detection and response capabilities Collaborate across GitLab teams to develop new security capabilities and deliver technical projects that enhance our infrastructure What you’ll bring  Demonstrated ability to learn and lead incident response processes independently Experience with SIEM/security logging tools Experience with cloud platforms (GCP and/or AWS) Experience building tools or automation with AI, and the judgment to test and verify what it produces (Python, SOAR, or other scripting is a plus) A passion for technical documentation Proactive approach to identifying and investigating security threats Interest in conducting forensic analysis of infected hosts Experience or strong desire to learn cloud-based security investigations Due to government requirements, you must be a United States Citizen (defined as any individual who is a citizen of the United States by law, birth, or naturalization) to fill this position.   About the team Security Operations is a globally distributed team of engineers split across 3 core regions; AMER, APAC and EMEA, and is at the forefront of security events that impact both GitLab.com and GitLab. We are both reactive and proactive, leading security investigations, incident response support and response resolution, through to cyber threat analysis and detection and response engineering. Even though we’re a global team, we work together in a cross-regional manner and have automation and processes to facilitate collaboration when resolving incidents, handovers, and general collaboration for project work as well. descriptionAr: About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role We are looking for an Associate, GTM Finance to help drive Ramp’s next phase of growth. This role will be a key strategic partner to cross-functional teams helping shape both (1) what our financial goals are and (2) how we will achieve them. The GTM Finance team owns key decisions around how we allocate and prioritize Ramp’s time and resources, and we are looking for a stellar Associate to quickly take on a large scope. This is a high-impact position and represents a truly unique opportunity to join one of the country’s fastest-growing, pre-IPO startups at a time when it is critical for us to build scalable financial and operational processes, tooling, and infrastructure. What You'll Do Build and own detailed financial and operational models, ensuring the highest quality and accuracy Design and implement processes & systems to support and scale one of the industry’s fastest-growing GTM organizations Identify and develop KPIs; build dashboards to monitor performance and communicate insights to relevant stakeholders Lead planning analyses for cross-functional teams, evaluating tradeoffs across growth, efficiency, and resourcing Use data to influence and inform key strategic business, GTM, and Product decisions Partner closely with operators and functional leaders to translate strategy into execution What You Need 2-4 years of experience in Strategic Finance, Operations, Investment Banking, Management Consulting, Corporate Finance, or a similar analytical role, preferably in a high-growth technology environment Excellent financial modeling and quantitative / data analysis skills Extreme attention to detail with a high regard for precision Track record of developing and maintaining relationships with both internal and external partners A “get things done” mentality; you can dissect complex problems, identify solutions, and drive these solutions to completion with a high degree of autonomy Exceptional verbal and written communication skills Comfort operating in ambiguity and adapting to evolving priorities Nice-to-Haves Expertise with Looker, SQL, and/or Python Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global) Flexible PTO Centralized home-office equipment ordering Health and wellness stipend Budget for intra-office travel Weekly coffee stipend United States 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents One Medical annual membership 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year) Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay Pet insurance In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed) Canada Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life Life, AD&D, and disability coverage Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime) Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP) Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health United Kingdom Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay Referral Instructions If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf. Other notices Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @ Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process. descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. In business generation and expansion, you’ll be tasked with qualification of prospect and customer use cases, technical requirements discovery, leading demonstrations, solution identification and design, and collaborative work on proofs-of-concept (PoCs). For our existing customers, Solutions Engineers are part of a dedicated account team that advises the customer on technical best practices, implementation of Cloudflare products and features, and strategic guidance on internet security and performance. The role requires 20-30% travel to attend meetings with prospects or customers, attend conferences and other industry events, and to collaborate with your Cloudflare teammates. Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience Our Solutions Engineers come from a wide range of backgrounds: financial consulting, engineering, software development, product management, customer support, and project delivery. You appreciate the diversity of challenges in working with customers, and look forward to helping them realize the full promise of Cloudflare. On the Solutions Engineering team, you will find a collaborative environment where everyone brings different strengths and jumps in to help each other. Demonstrated experience with a scripting language (e.g. Python, JavaScript, Bash, Lua, Go) and a desire to expand those skills. Expertise in internet technologies: OSI Model layers 1-7, BGP, GRE, TCP/UDP, DNS (authoritative and recursive), HTTP(S), SSL / TLS. Familiarity with Zero Trust Framework and SASE related concepts. 12 years plus of experience in a customer-facing sales or consulting role. It’s incumbent on us to stay up to date not only with Cloudflare’s specific products, but with industry trends. A focus on learning, teaching, collaboration, mentorship, and growth, not only personally but also within the team and company. Aside from technical and collaborative skills, we place a high value on project management, relationship building, and EQ. You've built web applications before, or contributed to existing web applications in a meaningful way. You understand the role of a firewall, the difference between L3, L4, and L7 firewalls, and that ‘ACL’ doesn't always mean Anterior Cruciate Ligament. You're not afraid of command-line interfaces, RESTful APIs, or analyzing HTTP request and response in a browser’s web inspector. You can describe the differences between CSRF, XSS, and SQLi in detail, and Cloudflare's role in defending against them. Understanding of, or experience with, regulatory requirements such a PCI DSS, HIPAA, and SOC-2. An undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field. Reminder: this is not a strict requirement at all. Candidates from all walks of life are welcome. You can translate technical concepts and jargon for a wide variety of audiences: from systems engineers, to front-end developers, through to IT managers and C-levels in organizations. An overview of this role What does software planning look like when people and artificial intelligence agents work together? As a Staff Product Manager for Planning at GitLab, you'll help answer that question and lead the team toward a clear product direction. This isn't just about improving traditional agile planning. You'll rethink how intent becomes actionable work, how that work moves through software development, and where human involvement is needed. You'll develop a point of view on planning's future and turn it into product decisions with engineering, design, and product leadership. That includes exploring how planning could connect work to business priorities and budgets, rather than assuming the answer is already decided. Alongside that strategic work, you'll share ownership of existing planning capabilities with another product manager. We're opening this role at Staff level, with flexibility to consider Principal level based on your experience and scope of impact. What you'll do Define a clear direction for planning as software development shifts toward collaboration between people and artificial intelligence agents, and help the team move from open questions to concrete priorities. Shape how users capture intent, break it into actionable work, and determine which work can proceed autonomously and which needs human involvement. Evaluate whether and how planning should connect software delivery to company priorities, business objectives, and budgets. Share ownership of planning capabilities, including work items, boards, specifications, and portfolio planning, with a fellow product manager. Help define how that scope is divided. Work with engineering and design to translate product direction into a roadmap and improvements to planning workflows across GitLab. Communicate your recommendations clearly to senior leaders, challenge assumptions constructively, and lead the team through changes in direction. What you'll bring Experience leading product strategy and execution for software development, developer tools, or planning products, with the depth to make decisions in a specialized product area. A strong understanding of software development and development and operations (DevOps) workflows, including how planning decisions affect downstream delivery. The ability to form and defend a product point of view in an uncertain, changing market, while staying open to different ideas. Clear communication with technical teams and senior executives, including experience challenging leadership decisions constructively and building support for a direction. The ability to connect a forward-looking strategy to practical product decisions and work collaboratively across product, engineering, and design. About the team The Planning team builds the capabilities at the start of GitLab's software development workflow, including work items, boards, specifications, and portfolio planning. Decisions here affect how work moves through the rest of the platform, so the team's scope extends beyond standalone project management tools. You'll work alongside another product manager and partner with engineering and design across this product area. The division of product ownership is still being shaped, and you'll help define it. The hiring manager wants you to bring a different perspective, question established approaches, and challenge senior leaders constructively, with room to influence decisions beyond your immediate product scope. GitLab's mission is to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. Our platform brings software development, security, and operations together.   The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity . Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary. descriptionAr: As a Senior Platform Engineer at Coder, you will own the infrastructure Coder's own engineers build on every day. Our internal environments run the same deployment path we publish for customers, so when something does not hold up at our scale, we find it before a customer does. We avoid building anything so specific to ourselves that a customer could not run the same thing. Platform Engineering owns three areas. We run the internal environments our engineers develop in, the self-service environments our field teams use to demo Coder, and the release pipeline that publishes every Coder artifact. You will take ownership of components across these and stay accountable for how they behave in production after they ship. Our users are Coder’s engineers and field teams, and you’ll work with them to decide what to build and how we know it worked. What you'll do here Own one or more components of our Kubernetes platform end to end, from the Terraform and Flux configuration to how they run in production. Improve the platform's observability, so that metrics, logs and alerts land in one stack with a runbook behind every alert. Keep our Kubernetes clusters current, including version and add-on upgrades. Apply cost and performance efficiency to our infrastructure. Work on workspace isolation and container runtimes. Contribute to the release and publishing pipeline for coder/coder, including its workflows, signing and publish targets. Design for least privilege, with short-lived credentials and no shared static keys. Write an RFC when a change warrants one, and a pull request a reviewer can follow without decoding it. Mentor one or two engineers on the components you know best. Run pilots with named users, gather feedback, and measure adoption and time to a useful result (e.g. from request to an environment someone can actually demo on) Own docs, onboarding and support for what you ship. What we're looking for 4+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering, with direct ownership of production systems other people depend on. Strong technical depth across Linux, Kubernetes, containers and Infrastructure as Code, Terraform in particular. Production experience with at least one major public cloud. Most of our infrastructure runs on AWS. Hands-on experience operating Kubernetes clusters, including upgrades, add-ons, autoscaling and the failure modes that come with them. Experience building and owning CI/CD pipelines, and treating them as production software. A working understanding of IP networking and HTTP fundamentals. Has changed or retired a platform feature based on how people used it, or can describe how they would decide to. Good instincts for where cloud spend goes and what a change will cost. Clear written communication. Most of this team's work is agreed in a document before it is built. Bonus tacos if you have (Tacos? If you need an ice-breaker, ask how we say thanks by giving tacos!) GitOps at scale with Flux or Argo CD. Prometheus, Grafana or OpenTelemetry, including alerts you defined and owned. Sandboxed container runtimes such as Kata, gVisor or sysbox. Release engineering, artifact signing or supply chain security. Prior work on developer tooling or internal developer platforms. Public open source contributions. You still carve out time to code, either at work or on passion projects. Our tech stack Backend: Go, Postgres, Kubernetes, gRPC Infrastructure: AWS, Terraform, Flux, Helm Observability: Prometheus, Grafana CI/CD: GitHub Actions General: GitHub, Slack, Discord, Notion About Coder Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. Coder provides self-hosted, agent-ready workspaces that unify developer productivity and platform governance. With Coder, enterprises can confidently evolve from human-only development to AI-assisted and autonomous workflows, without sacrificing security, compliance, or performance. Learn more at coder.com . Interview process We believe that the interview process should be transparent, consistent, and enjoyable. We value your time and hope to complete the interview process in two to four weeks, if schedules allow. Through your interviews, you will meet a mix of individual contributors, managers, and senior leaders. AI use during the interview process As an AI company, Coder embraces the use of AI tools, and we want to be transparent about our expectations as you navigate our interview process. Not permitted : Using AI assistance during conversational interviews. Permitted : Using AI tooling for take-home assessments. Please flag where and to what extent it was used in your take-home. Your submission will not be penalized for using AI as long as it is done honestly. Our use of AI in hiring We use AI tools to help manage our recruitment process efficiently and fairly.
