descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: United States: Austin, TX; San Francisco, CA; New York City; Washington D.C. United Kingdom: London About the Role Cloudforce One is Cloudflare’s threat operations and research team, responsible for identifying and disrupting cyber threats ranging from sophisticated cyber criminal activity to nation-state sponsored advanced persistent threats (APTs).  Cloudforce One works in close partnership with external organizations and internal Cloudflare teams, continuously developing operational tradecraft and expanding ever-growing sources of threat intelligence to enable expedited threat hunting and remediation.  Members of Cloudforce One are at the helm of leveraging an incredibly vast and varied set of data points that only one of the world’s largest global networks can provide.  The team is able to analyze these unique data points, at massive scale and efficiency, synthesizing findings into actionable threat intelligence to better protect our customers. As a Software Engineer on this team, you will own the entire software development lifecycle—from design and architecture to deployment and monitoring—for systems that serve both threat disruption and legal response efforts. You will be responsible for translating complex legal and security requirements into robust, scalable, and high-performance applications that have a direct impact on making the internet better, safer, and more powerful every day. Responsibilities While the majority of our services are now written in Golang and TypeScript, you will also work with technologies such as Rust, Kafka, Redis, Kubernetes, Terraform, Temporal and PostgresSQL. We also pride ourselves in dogfooding our own products and services so you will be extensively working with Cloudflare’s developer platform as well. We are looking for great engineers regardless of experience with any of these specific technologies. This role may require flexibility to be on-call outside of standard working hours to address technical issues as needed. Design, build, run, and scale distributed tools and services that support both cyber threat disruption and platform abuse efforts. Develop critical data pipelines and services to collect, analyze, and expose threat intelligence data for Cloudforce One analysts and Cloudflare customers, helping to identify Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs) and Indicators of Compromise (IOCs). Collaborate closely with Threat Intelligence, Trust & Safety, Legal, and Product teams to understand goals and translate complex technical requirements into elegant, scalable solutions. Improve system design and architecture to ensure stability, performance, and maintainability of both internal and customer-facing compliance and security services. Analyze, communicate, and help prioritize complex technical concepts across teams. Ongoing monitoring and maintenance of production services, including participation in on-call rotations. Mentor and guide other developers in the team, helping to build collective technical expertise and promote best practices for writing well-tested, modular, and reusable code. An overview of this role GitLab’s Forward Deployed Engineering team is a field-situated product engineering function focused on strategic customer outcomes, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, and direct contributions to GitLab’s product. This isn't a traditional field engineering, solutions architecture, or professional services role. As a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll work closely with customers while maintaining the technical standards and contribution discipline of a Staff-level product engineer. You'll work where strategic customer urgency, complex technical ambiguity, and GitLab product execution intersect. You'll partner directly with strategic customers and teams across Product, Engineering, Support, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Solutions Architecture (SA), Customer Success Architecture (CSA), Customer Success Management (CSM), and Professional Services. Why this role exists Strategic customers sometimes encounter challenges that are too broad, deep, urgent, or cross-functional for any single team to own from start to finish. These challenges may involve product gaps, performance degradation, scale bottlenecks, AI governance, adoption blockers, architectural constraints, Git usage patterns, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) complexity, application programming interface (API) automation, security requirements, or operational instability. Forward Deployed Engineering provides technical stewardship in these moments. The team doesn't simply observe, report, or escalate. You'll engage directly, diagnose the underlying technical problem, collaborate with the right teams, contribute code or technical solutions where appropriate, and transition the outcome into normal ownership once the customer is stable and the learning can be reused. What you’ll do Product contribution Contribute production-quality code to GitLab’s product and adjacent systems. Develop bug fixes, features, integrations, tooling, and performance improvements when strategic customer outcomes require direct engineering work. Work within GitLab’s product and engineering processes, including issue discovery, merge request creation, testing, review, documentation, and maintainability. Partner with Product and Engineering so customer-driven solutions support long-term product direction rather than becoming one-off customizations. Turn blockers discovered in the field into durable product improvements, reference architectures, documentation, and repeatable implementation patterns. Strategic technical stewardship Engage with strategically important customers when adoption, retention, executive confidence, or public trust is materially at risk. Diagnose complex problems across GitLab product behavior, customer architecture, Git internals, CI/CD workflows, API usage, observability, infrastructure, networking, and cloud environments. Coordinate across Product, Engineering, SRE, Support, SA, CSA, CSM, Professional Services, and customer technical teams to drive resolution from discovery through handoff. Provide recommendations grounded in data, traces, and systems analysis to improve GitLab usage, workflows, automation, and architecture. Create durable outcomes without establishing permanent dependency on Forward Deployed Engineering. AI adoption and agentic software development lifecycle Drive governed, measurable, and production-oriented adoption of GitLab Duo Agent Platform with strategic customers. Identify and resolve AI adoption blockers involving governance, usage controls, auditability, security, compliance, operating models, workflow design, and integrations. Develop customer-safe adoption patterns for the agentic software development lifecycle (SDLC), AI-assisted development, intent-based review, AI governance, and human-in-the-loop software delivery. Partner with Product, Engineering, Field, and Customer Success teams to turn AI adoption learning into reusable guidance and product improvements. Thought leadership Create technical narratives grounded in customer experience and product reality that can help shape the industry’s approach. Contribute to Well-Architected Frameworks, whitepapers, webinars, reference architectures, technical strategy memos, and adoption frameworks. Guide ideas through discovery, formulation, validation, amplification, and adoption across GitLab. Partner with SA, CSA, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Product Marketing Management, CSM

descriptionAr: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. An overview of this role As a Customer Success Architect, you’ll sit at the intersection of business outcomes and technical excellence, helping customers align GitLab’s DevSecOps platform with their strategic goals. You’ll act as a trusted advisor to key accounts, using your deep understanding of Git, CI/CD, software development lifecycles, and DevSecOps practices to guide them through complex challenges and drive adoption, utilization, and maturity across the GitLab platform. You’ll own a book of customers, translate pre-sales command plans into actionable success plans, and partner closely with Customer Success, Product Management, Engineering, Sales, Support, and Professional Services to ensure issues are resolved, value is realized, and long-term relationships grow. In this role, you’ll focus on the themes of align, enable, and expand: aligning our solutions to customer objectives, enabling teams through hands-on technical onboarding and best-practice guidance, and expanding value as customers progress on their GitLab journey. In your first year, you’ll be expected to build strong, consultative relationships, increase product adoption and customer satisfaction within your accounts, and become the go-to liaison for questions, escalations, and roadmap conversations. What you’ll do Partner with customers to translate pre-sales command plans into clear, actionable objectives tied to their desired business outcomes. Guide customers on how to best use the GitLab platform, applying DevSecOps, CI/CD, and Git best practices across common use cases. Lead customers through their adoption journey, from onboarding and enablement to ongoing utilization and maturity of the platform. Own a portfolio of customers, focusing on driving product adoption, retention, expansion, and overall satisfaction. Act as the primary GitLab liaison for your accounts, coordinating with Support, Product Management, Sales, and Professional Services on questions, issues, roadmaps, and escalations. Build and maintain Customer Success Plans with assigned customers, defining critical goals and key performance indicators, and track progress against those goals. Program manage account escalations, ensuring timely coordination, communication, and resolution across GitLab teams and customer stakeholders. Stay current on GitLab releases and new features, and proactively provide insights and recommendations on how customers can use them to achieve their objectives. Identify and recommend training and services opportunities that support customer enablement and long-term success. What you’ll bring Proven experience in customer success, post-sales, or professional services roles with a focus on driving adoption, retention, and measurable business outcomes. Practical understanding of Git, common branching strategies, and the software development lifecycle, including continuous integration, continuous deployment, and DevSecOps practices. Ability to act as a trusted advisor to technical and business stakeholders, partnering with customers to define, prioritize, and achieve their desired outcomes. Strong communication skills, including clear written and verbal communication, effective presentations, and the ability to explain technical topics to varied audiences. Demonstrated project management capabilities, including organizing work, managing escalations, and coordinating across internal teams such as Support, Product Management, Sales, and Services. Analytical and problem-solving skills to interpret customer data, identify risks or opportunities, and recommend actionable next steps. Comfort working both independently and as part of a distributed team, with attention to detail and alignment to GitLab’s values. Openness to travel as needed and to apply transferable skills from related roles or industries in support of customer success and technical enablement. Fluent French About the team The Customer Success Architect team focuses on hands-on technical enablement, adoption, utilization, and maturity of the GitLab DevSecOps platform while maintaining strong, consultative customer relationships and business alignment. You’ll work as part of a globally distributed, all-remote team that collaborates asynchronously with Customer Success Managers, Product Management, Engineering, Sales, Professional Services, and Support to act as a trusted advisor for customers. Our mission is to align GitLab capabilities with customer business outcomes, guide them along their adoption journey, and help them navigate complex technical and organizational change so they realize long-term value from GitLab. Locations: Austin TX, Champaign IL, Lisbon Portugal, London England, Atlanta GA, Washington DC,  About the team Cloudflare is redefining the way networks are run at scale, and some of the largest networks in the world now run their traffic through us. Cloudflare's network runs in hundreds of cities on general-purpose Linux servers, not dedicated routers, so the routers, firewalls, load balancers, and proxies that carry our customers' traffic are software that we write, ship, and operate ourselves. Our Packet Processing team builds and operates that software: high-performance code that processes customer traffic at the packet level as it moves through Cloudflare's network, in every Cloudflare data center. That includes the L4 load balancer at the front door of every server, a per-customer routing and forwarding data plane, a stateful network firewall, and a TCP/UDP reverse proxy (the engines behind products like Magic Transit, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare Network Firewall, and Spectrum). We are a team of engineers who obsess over performance, correctness, and reliability at massive scale. We own what we build in production, a lot of our work happens close to the kernel and the NIC. About the role We're looking for engineers who want to build the software that forwards, filters, and load-balances packets for a meaningful fraction of the internet. If you've worked on routers, switches, firewalls, load balancers, or SDN data planes, and you'd like to do that in software, at Cloudflare's scale, this is the role. We're moving towards a unified data plane platform that all of our L3/L4 products share. Instead of each product having its own data path, with its own configuration, performance work, and failure modes, we build a feature once and every product gets it. Some of the things you'd work on: The shared platform: packet I/O, a graph of processing stages, per-core steering, per-customer isolation, and upgrades that don't drop traffic A userspace forwarding plane that gives each customer their own routing and forwarding, with traffic arriving and leaving over tunnels (GRE, IPsec) and direct connections A stateful packet firewall written in Rust: rule evaluation, rate limiting, intrusion detection, packet capture, and dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 An XDP-based L4 load balancer that touches nearly every connection into Cloudflare and forwards packets between servers and between data centers A fast path that uses XDP and eBPF to forward very large single flows at multiple Gbps Host networking: classifying each packet once and using that result everywhere on the server, instead of separate configs that can disagree Chasing down packet drops, latency, and throughput problems across a fleet of servers in hundreds of cities We write mostly Go and Rust (plus C for eBPF) on Linux, and the work ranges from XDP and the kernel network stack to userspace packet pipelines and the control planes that configure them. You'll build, deploy, and operate these systems on top of one of the largest edge networks in the world. You'll partner with some of the best engineers and product managers, on our team and across Cloudflare, to solve big problems that have a meaningful impact in the lives of our customers and users. We're looking for curious, empathetic engineers who are excited to join us in changing the way networking is done! Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. About the Role: Millions of people rely on Notion to do their most important work, and protecting that trust is foundational to everything we build. Notion is flexible, powerful and always evolving. It is a product that needs to scale to meet the needs of many thousands of businesses globally. Those customers rely on us to protect their data and their customers’ data. This is where you come in — to help us forge a strong, reliable path forward to the future. Notion is looking for a risk analyst who has a passion for partnering with teams across the organization to envision, plan and enhance Notion's risk management posture. This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission. The Treasury team is responsible for protecting liquidity, enabling scale, maintaining strong controls, and helping the company operate with clarity and resilience. We work across finance and operational partners to ensure funds move safely, visibility remains high, and Treasury infrastructure keeps pace with a fast-moving business. As hands-on operators and builders, we combine financial judgment with AI, automation, and data to solve problems faster, strengthen controls, and continuously improve how Treasury operates. About the Role We are looking for a senior hire to help structure financing for major deals, improve working capital, and lead cash forecasting and liquidity planning. Reporting to the Treasurer, you’ll partner with Compute and teams across OpenAI to design creative financing and payment solutions that support the company’s growth. AI and automation will be core to how you build and scale this capability. This role can be based in San Francisco, CA, Seattle, WA, or New York, NY. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: Structure and negotiate trade finance solutions that improve deal economics and manage risk. Improve cash conversion by working with Billing, Collections, Accounting, and business teams to bill sooner, collect faster, improve supplier terms, and reduce unnecessary deposits or inventory commitments. Free up cash and credit capacity by managing collateral, letters of credit, guarantees, and renewals. Build direct cash forecasts by incorporating business-specific receipts and payments, compute commitments, and financing timing. Partner with Treasury’s Investment team to determine liquidity buffers, investment decisions, and contingency funding plans. Advise on deal structuring Compute, Finance, and Legal, then coordinate execution with Treasury Operations. Improve e-commerce payment economics with Product, Payments, and Strategic Finance, balancing cost, acceptance, risk, and settlement timing. Recommend billing, collection, prepayment, and credit terms for new business models, balancing cash protection with ease of purchase. Use AI and automation to streamline contract review, credit support tracking, cash forecasting, and treasury workflows. descriptionAr: Hi 👋🏻 I’m Louis, Head of Security. We’re building out the security function at Ashby. What Ashby gives you in return is the best of both early and growth-stage environments. The agency and no-nonsense approach of a seed startup: you write product specs, make product and design decisions, and build in an almost-no-meeting culture. The product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup: 100,000+ weekly active users who depend on your software and eagerly await your next feature. We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. You’ll join our Security team, a single team with multiple specializations overseeing security across the business. I report to Abhik, our Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. We’re bubbling with ideas for how to support Talent Acquisition with software, and we recently launched Talent Management products to expand our total addressable market and become a company worth $60B+. We read every application and aim to respond to yours within 3-4 days (often sooner). Role Overview An employee’s access is increasingly also the access they can delegate to an AI tool. That makes identity and permissions an engineering problem with a practical question behind it: can we understand what someone or their agent can reach, and reconstruct what happened when something goes wrong? We’re looking for someone who can build the systems that answer that question. You’ll automate access management, connect the evidence needed for investigations, and improve the security workflows our team uses every day. You’ll care about how those controls feel to the people using them as well as the risks they address. About the Role and How We Work Your mission is to automate and scale internal security access management while giving us the visibility and response capability to investigate incidents. You’ll own security integrations, identity workflows, operational telemetry, and automation across the internal environment, and incident management for the Security team. You’ll work closely with IT on access management and logging, with Engineering on service and agent identities, with Infrastructure on cloud signals, and with GRC on control requirements and AI governance evidence. GRC will run routine vendor diligence; you’ll provide deeper technical review when data sensitivity, privileged access, integration scope, or service criticality warrants it. You’ll own the security logic and automation connecting these systems and be the Security team’s sole owner for incident management. You’ll lead intake, triage, coordination, escalation, and follow-through. Application Security will own product authorization and AI-feature threat modeling and contribute specialist analysis during incidents. Together, you’ll make internal access decisions and investigations coherent across human, service, and agent activity. In practice, you’ll: Automate identity lifecycle and access changes, including joiner, mover, and leaver workflows, access reviews, expiring grants, and integrations with internal systems. Help define prohibited combinations of role, system, action, and data, then implement access controls and monitoring proportionate to the risk. Evaluate and extend contextual access controls that assess each request using current identity, device posture, and relevant behavioral signals. Compare how Okta and Cloudflare can support those decisions across internal systems. Centralize useful telemetry from identity, SaaS, infrastructure, repositories, and data systems. Define and maintain detections and escalation rules with our outsourced SOC, improving them through incident learnings. Evaluate SIEM options through a practical proof of concept, including Datadog Cloud SIEM, Microsoft Sentinel, and Splunk, then recommend an approach based on coverage, investigation quality, effort, and cost. Build agent attribution: connect the initiating human, acting agent, credentials and permissions, trigger, and resulting actions so activity can be reconstructed. Deliver useful alerts and permitted response actions through Slack, with access checks, confirmation where needed, and an audit trail. Use AI to help with enrichment and triage while retaining accountability for consequential decisions. Own incident management from preparation and intake through severity assessment, containment and recovery coordination, stakeholder updates, post-incident review, and tracking follow-up actions to closure. Build the evidence capture, playbooks, and automation that make investigations faster and more reliable. To ground it with examples, you could: Build an access workflow that grants an appropriate capability for a limited period and automatically removes it, with the reason and owner attached. Follow an agent’s repository or infrastructure action back to the human who initiated it and show the permissions it used. Connect identity and SaaS events to an alert that gives an investigator enough context to act, then test whether the detection works without flooding the team with routine activity. Why You Should and Shouldn’t Apply You should apply if: You’ve built integrations, internal tools, or automation for identity, security operations, or enterprise systems, and you can write maintainable code. You understand authentication, authorization, least privilege, and how access and delegation work across cloud and SaaS systems. You’ve worked with logs, detections, and incident investigations, coordinated a security incident through resolution, and know what evidence a responder needs to reconstruct an event. You care about the experience of employees using security controls, and you can use data to stage changes and find workflows that need a better path. descriptionAr: About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role Ramp is building a more intelligent, scalable go-to-market engine. As an Associate on the GTM Operations team, you’ll combine analytical rigor with hands-on process design, systems thinking, and AI-enabled automation to help our GTM teams execute more effectively. You’ll work directly with GTM leaders and cross-functional partners to identify performance gaps, turn insights into operating improvements, and build repeatable workflows that scale. This is a high-velocity individual contributor role with broad ownership: you’ll define problems, build solutions, and measure their impact. Your primary focus will be defined by the team you support, with shared standards and close partnership across Strategic Finance, Growth Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, GTM Systems, and Data. What You'll Do Lead cross-functional projects beyond these core operating areas, taking ambiguous problems through implementation, stakeholder adoption, and impact measurement. Diagnose pipeline, conversion, and rep-execution gaps; partner with leaders to prioritize interventions and measure their impact. Partner with GTM leaders to improve segmentation, account books, and territory design, aligning coverage with customer needs and team capacity. Strengthen attribution definitions, logic, and data quality so leaders can reliably connect GTM activities to outcomes. Partner with Product and Growth to enhance sales tools that improve rep efficiency and coverage. What You Need 2-4 years of relevant experience in GTM Strategy and Operations, Management Consulting, Investment Banking, or similar analytical role, preferably in a high-growth technology environment Demonstrated ability to turn insights into scalable processes, systems, and automation, owning execution from design through rollout and delivering measurable gains in adoption, productivity, and GTM performance. Exceptional verbal and written communication skills; ability to explain analytical findings, recommend a course of action, and align stakeholders. The ability to prioritize high-leverage work, manage multiple projects, and follow through from a loosely defined problem to a reliable operating solution. Nice-to-Haves Ability to partner across Sales, Finance, Product, and post-sale teams to support multiple GTM motions in a multiproduct business, translating shared priorities into clear decisions, coordinated execution, and measurable results. Familiarity with product-led, usage-based, or consumption-driven GTM motions. Demonstrated ability to drive adoption of new tools and processes through documentation, enablement, and change management. Hands-on experience with Salesforce and a BI platform such as Looker, including familiarity with CRM data structures, funnel reporting, and data-quality controls. Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global) Flexible PTO Centralized home-office equipment ordering Health and wellness stipend Budget for intra-office travel Weekly coffee stipend United States 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents One Medical annual membership 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year) Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay Pet insurance In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed) Canada Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life Life, AD&D, and disability coverage Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime) Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP) Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health United Kingdom Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay Referral Instructions If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf. descriptionAr: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role As a Revenue Technology Manager at GitLab, you'll lead how the tools we build and buy work together as we grow our consumption-based business. You'll own the vision, roadmap, and requirements for internal go-to-market applications, starting with Command Center, which helps field teams act on product usage and consumption data. You'll decide what those applications need to do and how they should fit with the rest of the stack. Engineering will own their technical architecture, code, and infrastructure. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports, reporting to the Director, Revenue Technology, within Revenue Operations. What you’ll do Define how internal and third-party tools fit together, including integrations, data flows, and governance, in partnership with the people who manage each tool. Recommend when to build, buy, or consolidate tools based on cost, return on investment, and how well each option meets the needs of go-to-market teams. Own the roadmap for Command Center and other internal applications. Turn requests from Sales, Solutions Architecture, Customer Experience, Product, and Ecosystem into clear requirements, and explain what you won't prioritize and why. Partner with Engineering to deliver applications that fit the existing stack and limit technical debt. Lead user acceptance testing, launch, documentation, and enablement, then use adoption data to decide what to improve, expand, or retire. Set the long-term direction of the revenue technology stack with Revenue Strategy, Revenue Operations, and field leaders as the business and artificial intelligence capabilities evolve. Build artificial intelligence and automation workflows that save time for Revenue Technology and go-to-market teams, and help the team decide when to use them. Bring consumption metrics into the tools and workflows field teams rely on, and adapt them as GitLab's consumption model matures. What you’ll bring Experience in Revenue Operations, Sales or Customer Success Operations, business systems, or a related role, with ownership of tools from defining the use case and choosing a solution through launch. Experience designing or guiding a go-to-market technology stack, including how tools connect and share data through application programming interfaces, integrations, data models, and permissions. Working knowledge of Salesforce, product usage data, and revenue tools such as Gainsight, Clari, Gong, or Outreach. Hands-on experience with a consumption- or usage-based business model, including how teams use consumption metrics across the customer lifecycle. Experience delivering internal tools with engineering teams, including writing scoped requirements and acceptance criteria and running user acceptance testing before release. Experience making build-versus-buy or consolidation decisions based on cost, return on investment, and business fit. You can reconcile competing requests from senior stakeholders and explain your decisions clearly. Experience shipping artificial intelligence agents or workflows people rely on, with the judgment to know where automation helps and where it adds complexity. Strong written communication in an all-remote, asynchronous environment. You can prioritize your work, keep teammates informed, and collaborate through issues, documents, and merge requests. Experience querying data directly with Structured Query Language (SQL) or a comparable tool, working with go-to-market analytics, or supporting field enablement is helpful, not required. We welcome transferable skills from related roles. About the team Revenue Technology owns the tools GitLab's go-to-market teams use, whether we build them or buy them. We're a globally distributed team that works asynchronously and partners with Revenue Operations, Revenue Strategy, Enablement, IT, and Engineering to support Sales, Customer Success, Professional Services, and Ecosystem teams. We put decisions in writing and focus on making the tools easier for field teams to use.   Remote-Global The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity

descriptionAr: About the Team The Model Policy team within OpenAI’s Safety Systems organization defines how increasingly capable AI models should behave in real-world settings. We turn research on emerging risks into model behavior policies, evaluations, and safeguards. About the Role As AI systems become more capable, the same advances that expand their legitimate uses can also lower barriers to harm. Emerging misuse risks range from AI assistance with conventional weapons development and the misuse of AI-enabled robotics to fraud, impersonation, and other forms of abuse that people can carry out at scale using AI agents. You’ll build threat models for how people could misuse AI in digital and physical settings, assess what access to AI changes in practice, and use that evidence to define how models should respond. This role is based in San Francisco. We offer relocation support and work from the office three days a week, with optional work from home on Thursdays and Fridays. In this role, you will: Build and update threat models as capabilities evolve. Assess what people could plausibly do, what expertise and resources they would need, and how AI changes those barriers. Define when models should help, limit assistance, or refuse in situations where the same capability has legitimate and harmful uses. Turn expert safety judgment into instructions, training examples, and evaluations that teach models when to help, when to limit assistance, and when to refuse. Turn threat models into evaluation scenarios and grading guidance. Analyze model outputs, red-team findings, and deployment data to identify where models enable misuse or block legitimate work. Partner with research, engineering, security, and product teams to apply findings to model training, deployment decisions, and monitoring. You might thrive in this role if you: Have hands-on experience building, testing, or assessing dual-use technologies, or a track record of threat modeling grounded in how people use and misuse real systems. Demonstrate deep practical experience in one relevant domain and the judgment to know when to bring in experts from others. Are able to assess whether a capability demonstrated in a test materially changes what someone could do outside it. Can translate technical evidence and uncertainty into clear policy boundaries and measurable evaluation criteria. Have experience analyzing gold sets, evaluation results, and training data to spot inconsistent human labels, assess how annotator disagreement affects measured performance, and decide what to investigate next. Are comfortable working hands-on with model data and evaluation results, including inspecting examples, analyzing failure patterns, assessing data quality, and distinguishing policy failures from grader, model, or system failures. Use empirical evidence to develop and refine safety policies and safeguards. Work well across disciplines and revises their judgment as capabilities and evidence change. Enjoy fast-paced, collaborative research environments where priorities shift as models, evidence, and risks change. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Lisbon, or London (Hybrid) About the Department Emerging Technologies & Incubation (ETI) is where new and bold products are built and released within Cloudflare. Rather than being constrained by the structures which make Cloudflare a hugely successful business, we are able to leverage them to deliver entirely new tools and products to our customers. Cloudflare’s edge and network make it possible to solve problems at massive scale and efficiency which would be impossible for almost any other organization. About the Team We build the products that enable the next era of the Internet: making domains Readable , Discoverable , and Callable for autonomous AI agents. Here at Cloudflare, agentic discovery is a core part of our vision for the Agentic Internet . As AI agents change how humans and machines find, evaluate, and act on information, businesses need tools to control how they are represented and reached. We build capabilities that enable website owners to prepare their sites for agent interaction, test and observe how agents read their content, establish open interaction standards (like WebMCP and MCP), and create entirely new channels to reach agentic audiences. We are a cross functional group that communicates and collaborates regularly. We celebrate our achievements, support each other when we make mistakes, and hold each other and our work to a high standard. About the Role We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to serve as a technical anchor and become a subject matter expert on our Agentic Discovery team. In this role, you will define the architecture, core protocols, and multi-team standards powering the next generation of agent-web interactions. As a senior technical leader, you will shape product roadmaps, mentor engineers across Cloudflare, and write technical specifications that drive execution across multiple teams. You will drive engineering excellence across edge infrastructure, data pipelines, protocol layers, and developer tooling, ensuring systems are resilient and complexity is reduced for your peers. What You'll Do Architect and ship high-throughput, resilient production services that make web properties Readable (structured content transformation), Discoverable (indexing and AEO), and Callable (WebMCP, tool-calling APIs, Generative UI) for autonomous agents. Define emerging agent protocols and integrations (MCP, MCP Apps, UCP, MPP, WebMCP). Author architectural specifications and technical designs that guide engineering work both within and outside the ETI team. Partner directly with Product Management, customers and stakeholders to translate customer needs into technical requirements, clarify KPIs, and shape engineering roadmaps. Drive improvements in system health and observability. Lead complex incident responses, conduct post-incident retrospectives, and rearchitect systems to eliminate failure modes and minimize customer-escalation issues. Elevate the engineering process across Cloudflare through code reviews, technical mentorship, architectural governance, and candidate evaluation for engineering hiring. Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience Experience designing scalable system architecture and setting performance metrics in a distributed environment. Experience writing technical specifications and leading cross-functional technical initiatives to completion. Deep understanding of HTTP, APIs, proxies, caching, web security, and performance bottlenecks spanning multi-service architectures. Hands-on experience and deep conceptual understanding of AI agents, tool calling, Model Context Protocol (MCP), or agent harnesses. Ability to partner with product managers and customers to navigate ambiguous problem spaces and iteratively deliver large-scale architecture. Experience mentoring junior and mid-level engineers, contributing to hiring, and driving improvements to engineering processes and incident response workflows. descriptionAr: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role As a Journey Architect on GitLab's Digital Customer Outcomes team, you'll design journeys that turn meaningful customer actions into retention, consumption and revenue outcomes. You'll own journey design and service blueprints for assigned customer cohorts, products or coverage models, leading cross-functional work from design through launch. Digital Orchestration builds and runs the journeys day to day; you'll remain accountable for their outcomes and ongoing improvement. You'll add design capacity to help priority journeys, including artificial intelligence (AI) and consumption journeys, launch in fiscal year 2028 (FY28). What you’ll do Design journeys backward from business outcomes to meaningful customer actions, audiences and engagement tactics. Map each cohort's intended path, timing, signals that customers need help and interventions to get them back on track. Decide which steps are self-serve, AI-assisted or human-led, and define the handoffs between them. Design across in-product guidance, email, events and community, choosing the right channel for each moment. Build service blueprints with Customer Experience (CX) Operations, documenting the people, systems, data, content and handoffs behind each touchpoint. Give every step a trigger, a response, an owner and a metric. Write journey specifications covering steps, triggers, audiences, channels, content, handoffs and metrics. Set build plans, coordinate partner teams and clear dependencies to launch on time and to specification. Specify the content and self-service resources each step needs, and work with content teams to create and govern them. Partner with Lifecycle Marketing on audience, sequencing and delivery so customers experience one coordinated journey. Hand live journeys to Digital Orchestration to run, remain accountable for their outcomes and build in regular optimization cycles with the Digital Outcomes team's Data/Insights partner. Measure journey coverage, step conversion, lift against comparison groups, meaningful actions, recovery after interventions, time to value and influence on retention. Track partner adoption of the shared journeys and blueprints. Apply the framework and standards set by the Lead Journey Architect, and help improve them based on what your journeys teach the team. What you’ll bring Experience in customer journey design, service design or digital customer success. A track record of turning journey designs into launched programs with measurable outcomes. Hands-on experience building service blueprints and designing handoffs between digital and human teams. Working knowledge of journey orchestration, in-app guidance and marketing automation platforms. Comfort defining customer signals and success metrics, and interpreting funnel conversion and test results. Experience leading cross-functional work through launch without direct authority. Experience in business-to-business software as a service is helpful, as is domain knowledge of development and operations (DevOps) or development, security and operations (DevSecOps). Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application. About the team The Digital Customer Outcomes team brings digital experiences and human support together around customer outcomes. You'll work day to day with the Lead Journey Architect, Digital Orchestration and the Digital Outcomes team's Data/Insights partner, alongside CX Operations, Lifecycle Marketing, Marketing Engineering and Operations, Content, Product, CX Engineering, Customer Success, Renewals and CX Services. You'll bring these partners together around shared journeys and blueprints so customer touchpoints line up rather than compete.       How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being Flexible Paid Time Off  Team Member Resource Groups Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan Growth and Development Fund Parental Leave   Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI’s mission is to build safe artificial general intelligence (AGI) which benefits all of humanity. This long-term undertaking brings the world’s best scientists, engineers, and business professionals into one lab together to accomplish this. The GTM Agentic Workflows team is building OpenAI’s agentic go-to-market operating system. We work with sellers, GTM leaders, and partners in GTM Systems, Data Science, and Product to connect customer intelligence to account strategy, helping teams prioritize opportunities, grow adoption across accounts, and spend time where it matters most. About the Role As an individual contributor on the GTM Agentic Workflows team, you’ll own the design, rollout, and performance of processes and workflows across the customer lifecycle, from lead routing through deal execution, delivery, and consumption. Orchestration is central to this role. You’ll bring sellers, GTM leaders, and cross-functional partners together around a shared outcome, then connect the work of people, systems, and agentic workflows to deliver it. In this role, you will: Prioritize problems with GTM leaders and the field. Look at where sellers repeat work, where deals stall, and which handoffs break down. Use the frequency and impact of those problems to decide what to tackle first. Strengthen the foundations of GTM workflows. Set the strategy for enriching person and company data, and partner with GTM Systems on lead routing and how sellers manage accounts and opportunities in Salesforce. Orchestrate delivery across teams. Align owners on the outcome, sequence work across functions, and resolve competing priorities. Make clear who decides, what information carries forward, and when the next team can act. Design and launch workflows with Product and Enterprise Systems. Define what triggers the workflow, what information an agent needs, and when a person should review or approve an action. Pilot with field teams and partner with Enablement on rollout. Own performance after launch. Measure adoption alongside outcomes such as lead response time, accuracy of proposed updates, and time to complete a handoff. Use those results and field feedback to decide what to improve next. You might thrive in this role if you have: 8+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or related roles at a high-growth technology company Strong systems thinking with deep experience designing and scaling sales systems, processes, and workflows across the full sales lifecycle Experience taking a multi-step GTM workflow from a field problem through rollout. You can explain what you automated, where people retained judgment, and how you measured whether it worked. Strong proficiency in Salesforce and data tools (e.g., SQL, Excel). Strong analytical skills with high attention to detail Experience with territory design, account structures, and pipeline management A track record of leading through influence. You can point to a cross-functional initiative where you brought teams with competing priorities to a decision and saw it through to delivery. Ability to operate in ambiguity, prioritize effectively, and manage multiple high-impact initiatives simultaneously About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement . Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form . No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link . OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. Join us in shaping the future of technology.

An overview of this role As a Principal Revenue Strategist, you'll help shape how GitLab brings its products to market as artificial intelligence changes how software is built and bought. Reporting to the VP of Revenue Strategy, you'll be a senior individual contributor connecting market, product, and field insights to clear recommendations and changes in how we sell. You'll take on complex, open-ended go-to-market questions with limited context, working directly with executive partners across Sales, Finance, and Product to decide where to invest, how to reach customers, and what needs to change. What you'll do Shape revenue strategy across customer segmentation, sales coverage, sales motions, and investment priorities. Design multi-quarter changes in how we sell and monetize, defining the implications for the customer journey, metrics, roles, incentives, and operating model. Build agreement on the path forward and partner with Field Operations and Enablement on execution. Develop market and expansion strategies, prioritizing markets, defining go-to-market models and capacity needs, and identifying the operational dependencies of entering or scaling in new regions. Connect go-to-market strategy and Product by translating field and customer insights into product input, and product direction into commercial implications. Provide focused, commercially grounded input on pricing and packaging. Contribute strategic inputs to long-range planning, including total addressable market, sales capacity, productivity, and unit economics, while Field Operations and Finance retain ownership of annual planning, quota setting, and territory design. Build models, write decision memos, run analyses, and facilitate working sessions to turn recommendations into action with cross-functional partners. Advise senior leaders in Sales, Finance, and Product independently, distilling complex problems into clear recommendations with explicit assumptions and trade-offs. What you'll bring Experience owning complex go-to-market or revenue strategy work in a growing technology company, consulting, or a combination of both. Relevant experience and transferable skills matter more than a particular career path. Direct experience solving business-to-business software go-to-market problems, such as segmentation, coverage, pipeline and conversion, sales capacity and productivity, incentives, or pricing and packaging. A structured approach to testing assumptions and turning an unclear problem into a framework, a recommendation, and practical next steps. Strong commercial and analytical judgment, including the ability to build models and recognize when the evidence is sufficient to make a decision. The ability to work credibly with senior leaders, challenge decisions with evidence, and influence people without formal authority. A collaborative, hands-on approach that treats execution as part of strategy, not a handoff after the recommendation. Helpful, but not required: experience with usage-based or consumption models, international expansion, enterprise or platform sales, or a technical or scientific background. Interest in people management over time is welcome, but this is an individual contributor role. About the team The Revenue Strategy team tackles strategic questions about how GitLab reaches customers, sells, and monetizes its platform. You'll work with Sales, Finance, and Product leaders to connect strategy with commercial decisions, and with Field Operations and Enablement to put those decisions into practice. GitLab is an all-remote company with a public handbook and a transparent, low-ego culture. Our mission is to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI’s mission is to ensure the responsible and widespread adoption of artificial intelligence. In support of that mission, the SMB Marketing team helps small and medium-sized businesses understand and adopt ChatGPT Business and OpenAI’s B2B solutions. We build a deep understanding of business owners and teams, shape relevant product narratives, and drive awareness, adoption, and growth. We take a data-driven approach to understand SMB audiences, uncover customer needs, and translate AI capabilities into practical business value. We partner closely with Growth, Product Marketing, Sales, Partnerships, Product, Research, Communications, and Design to deliver a cohesive customer experience across discovery, evaluation, purchase, adoption, and expansion. About the Role We’re looking for a Product Marketing Manager, SMB to bring together SMB insights, market understanding, and product knowledge to shape positioning, inform product priorities, and deliver go-to-market initiatives that drive adoption and measurable business impact. You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering, Growth, and Partnerships to understand SMB needs, translate complex AI capabilities into clear customer value, and bring new products and features to market. This role is ideal for someone who combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution, independently navigates ambiguity, and brings cross-functional partners together to deliver results. In this role, you will: Define the product and marketing strategy for a component of OpenAI’s SMB portfolio in partnership with cross-functional partners Develop an actionable understanding of SMB segments, customer needs, buying behavior, and workflows through research, product usage, market analysis, and competitive insight to improve positioning, adoption, and product-market fit. Own positioning and messaging for your product area, translating complex capabilities into compelling narratives for different SMB owners and teams across relevant industries and business functions. Partner with Product and Engineering to bring customer needs and market insights into roadmap discussions and product decisions. Develop and drive go-to-market plans for new products and partner integrations, owning marketing execution from planning through launch and ongoing adoption. Create SMB-facing content, including product narratives, workflow demos and webinar content, one-pagers, FAQs, and launch communications. Partner with Product Growth, Partnerships, and Data Science to define success metrics, assess launch and adoption performance, and turn findings into improvements. Surface launch risks related to performance, safety, policy, and trust, working with the relevant teams to address them in launch plans and customer communications. Align cross-functional partners around priorities, responsibilities, and timelines, making thoughtful tradeoffs and resolving blockers within your initiatives. Build repeatable approaches to launches, messaging, and enablement, sharing learnings and mentoring peers to improve the team’s storytelling and execution. You might thrive in this role if you are/have: Have experience independently developing product and marketing strategies and bringing products to market, particularly in SMB software, platforms, or data and AI. Have experience in structured problem solving environments including but not limited to strategy/management consulting, investment banking, corporate strategy and venture capital Understand SMB needs and the partner ecosystem, includingand the market landscape, including advertiser goals and the advertising ecosystem, including measurement, targeting and relevance, creative, auctions, and performance tradeoffs. Have strong understanding of SMB workflows and software adoption, with the ability to adapt product value to different industries, use cases, and customer needs. Experience with platforms, integrations, plug-ins, technology partnerships, or SMB ecosystem GTM. Can turn customer research and market insights into clear positioning, actionable go-to-market plans, and recommendations that inform product priorities. Communicate clearly and persuasively, translating technical concepts into differentiated positioning for a range of audiences. Use qualitative and quantitative evidence—including customer interviews, surveys, adoption data, and experiments—to make decisions and improve results. Bring structured problem solving and strong judgment to ambiguous challenges, independently setting priorities and managing initiatives from strategy through execution. Build effective partnerships across Product, Engineering, Growth, Partnerships, and other teams, influencing decisions and driving alignment without formal authority About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. An overview of this role As a Senior CX Platform Engineer, you'll help GitLab's Customer Experience (CX) teams hand real work to artificial intelligence (AI). You'll use Claude Code and GitLab Duo Agent Platform as your default development tools, designing agentic workflows and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers with production testing, security, and shared ownership. What you'll do Use Claude Code, GitLab Duo, and other coding agents as your primary development environment for planning, implementation, refactoring, testing, reviews, and documentation. Run multiple agents in parallel on well-scoped tasks, critically review their output, and own every line that reaches production. Build and maintain the team's agent harness, including shared AGENTS.md conventions, skills, slash commands, hooks, subagent definitions, and continuous integration checks. Measure and share what works, publish reusable patterns, and retire those that don't. Ship agents and multi-step workflows for account research, success planning, scoping, status reporting, and customer onboarding. Package them as skills and plugins for non-engineers using Claude, Claude in Slack, and GitLab Duo Agent Platform. Build MCP servers and connectors for governed access to GitLab, Salesforce, Gainsight, Kantata, Thought Industries, Gong, Snowflake, and other enterprise systems. Add evaluations, tracing, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints to keep internal and customer-facing agents measurable, auditable, and safe with customer data. Evolve the CX Application Platform's gateway, Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure, including Elastic Container Service (ECS), Relational Database Service (RDS), and Lambda, Terraform configuration, application scaffold, and deployment path. Own applications such as PS Compass, Congregate, and GitLab University and its integrations, documenting build-versus-buy and consolidate-or-sunset decisions. Ship production-quality Python and TypeScript through GitLab continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), with tests, observability, security review, and runbooks. Design every application for handoff, with documentation, monitoring, and shared ownership. Prototype with Customer Success, Digital Success, Professional Services, Education Services, and Training in days, not quarters. Help CX team members bring their own applications to production, and turn field learning into reusable reference implementations, development paths, and enablement. Contribute upstream to GitLab and share product feedback with Product and Engineering. Mentor engineers and non-engineers on agentic development and raise the team's code review bar. What you'll bring Experience building and operating production software, owning multi-quarter work from ambiguity to production, choosing reusable platform solutions over one-off customization where appropriate, and designing for handoff. Daily, hands-on use of coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitLab Duo, or similar on production work. You can show how they've changed what you ship and how you maintain quality. Experience building with large language models (LLMs) beyond chat, including tool use, MCP servers, agent loops, context and retrieval design, prompt and workflow design, and evaluations. Strong Python skills with FastAPI or Flask and TypeScript skills with Vue or React, including application programming interface (API) design, authentication, authorization, and secure handling of customer and business data. Hands-on experience with AWS ECS, RDS, and Lambda, Terraform, Docker, and applications running behind single sign-on (SSO), such as Okta. Experience integrating enterprise systems through Representational State Transfer (REST) and GraphQL APIs, and fluency with Git, merge requests, and CI/CD. Experience translating non-engineering stakeholders' workflows into technical plans and writing clear asynchronous design documents, decision records, and enablement materials. You align with GitLab's values and are willing to use GitLab for your own work. descriptionAr: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role As a Professional Services Technical Architect at GitLab, you'll lead the technical direction of customer engagements from early scoping and discovery through delivery. You'll design high-level architectures and implementation plans for GitLab infrastructure and functionality, and you'll make sure deliverables align with customer requirements and the Statement of Work (SOW). You'll coordinate and guide implementation work across GitLab Professional Services and partner consultants, support customers deploying GitLab in cloud and on-premises environments using tools like Terraform, Ansible, and the GitLab Environment Toolkit, and perform migrations to GitLab using Congregate. You'll provide DevOps and DevSecOps consulting and best practices, contribute reusable collateral such as documentation, delivery kits, and training materials, and share product release updates to help the team deliver consistent outcomes. This role combines deep technical expertise with customer-facing leadership in GitLab's remote, asynchronous, and values-driven environment. What you’ll do Designing and delivering GitLab reference architecture implementations for both self-managed and cloud environments, using infrastructure as code practices Leading source code management and CI/CD migrations to GitLab, including large-scale enterprise moves using Congregate Building repeatable delivery kits, documentation, and enablement materials that help Professional Services and partners deploy and adopt GitLab best practices Lead the full technical delivery lifecycle for GitLab Professional Services engagements, from early scoping and technical discovery through implementation and handoff. Produce high-level and detailed technical designs for GitLab infrastructure and functionality, ensuring deliverables align with customer requirements and expectations. Evaluate and communicate scalability and security considerations (including compliance constraints) in proposed GitLab reference architectures and implementation plans. Deploy and configure GitLab in customer environments, including on-premises and major cloud providers, using Terraform, Ansible, and the GitLab Environment Toolkit (GET) aligned to reference architectures. Plan and execute source system migrations to GitLab using Congregate, partnering closely with customer stakeholders to reduce risk, protect data integrity, and minimize downtime. Provide DevOps and DevSecOps consulting and best-practice guidance, including advising on internal frameworks such as the Delivery Governance Framework (DGF) and GitLab Flow. Coordinate and oversee implementation work across GitLab team members, partners, and customer points of contact (POCs), ensuring clear asynchronous communication and decision capture, effective execution, and high-quality outcomes. Mentor Professional Services and partner consultants by contributing documentation, delivery kits, and training materials, and by leading enablement sessions on how to deliver and position service offerings. Maintain and improve delivery automation assets with an emphasis on code cleanliness, maintainability, and appropriate unit/integration testing. Support scoping and Statement of Work (SOW) creation with Professional Services Engagement Managers, stay current on monthly GitLab releases, and help Regional Delivery Managers with technical vetting and staffing assessments while maintaining a 55% billable utilization. Review and provide input to Professional Services training materials and presentations Develop case studies, presentations, design documentation, and best-practice methodologies Work closely with customer project teams to ensure accurate task-level articulation of work required What you’ll bring Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to lead technical discussions with customers and partners and communicate risks/trade-offs clearly in an asynchronous environment. Prefer location in PST, MST or CST timezone alignment. Comfortable with up to 30% travel at times. Demonstrated experience delivering two or more of the following consulting services: source code management migration, cloud architecture, DevOps engineering, or continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) consulting services. Enterprise software development experience, with the ability to translate requirements into clear technical designs and implementation plans.Progressive DevOps platform experience, including designing and implementing reliable, scalable systems with clear performance and security trade-offs. Hands-on experience deploying and managing infra
